title: Molecular mechanisms underlying phenotypic overlap and AI-misclassification in rare bone diseases: Insights from SHOX-related signaling pathways in endochondral ossification.
authors: Fischer, Isabel; Bialdiga, Sina; Schmidt, Philipp; Bolmer, Eike; Javanmardi, Behnam; Mohnike, Klaus; Schanze, Denny
abstract: The diagnosis of rare bone diseases (RBDs) is challenged by their heterogeneity and rare occurrence. However, correct and timely diagnosis is highly relevant for the best therapeutic outcome of patients. We regarded two AI-approaches developed by the Bone2Gene project that aim to support the diagnostic process by assigning hand radiographs to RBDs. We noticed a predominant misclassification of several RBDs into the group of SHOX-related short stature. To find potential genetic explanations for this overlap, we performed a literature research for SHOX-related signaling in endochondral ossification and connections to the signaling underlying other RBDs. We found that SHOX activates the expression of the structural protein aggrecan (ACAN) and represses FGFR3-induced RAS/RAF/MAPK signaling, displaying signaling connections to ACAN-related growth disorder as well as Hypochondroplasia and Achondroplasia, respectively. Additionally, we conclude that the high phenotypic variety of SHOX-related short stature also contributes to the misclassification of RBDs that do not show a direct connection to SHOX-related signaling. Overall, we deepened our understanding of the occurrence of misclassification in both Bone2Gene approaches. Complemented with genetic testing, Bone2Gene can be a valuable tool in the diagnostic process of RBDs.

title: Immediate early response 3 promotes airway epithelial inflammation and represents a therapeutic target in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
authors: Yang, Yuanlan; Hu, Zhengyu; Wang, Wenjing; Wu, Mindan; Cui, Yachao; Chen, Zemin; Jin, Xuan; Huang, Wenfeng; Yan, Jiawei; Zhang, Feng; Yin, Wenguang; Cui, Jieda; Zhu, Leqing; Ran, Pixin; Dai, Jianwei
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent airway inflammation, yet clinically useful biomarkers and mechanistically validated therapeutic targets remain limited. Here, we aimed to identify and functionally validate smoke-responsive regulators of airway epithelial inflammation in COPD and establish an interpretable prediction framework by integrating population-based clinical data, multi-omics analyses, genetic causal inference, and experimental validation. METHODS: Complementary clinical and molecular investigations used separate populations. Interpretable machine-learning models classified recorded COPD status in CHARLS, with validation across survey waves. Independent lung transcriptomic analyses integrated differential expression, co-expression networks, 113 machine-learning configurations, and single-cell profiling. Two-sample Mendelian randomization examined genetically predicted IER3 expression in relation to FEV(1)/FVC. Functional effects of IER3 were evaluated through AAV-mediated silencing in cigarette-smoke-exposed mice and siRNA knockdown in cigarette-smoke-extract-stimulated bronchial epithelial cells. Drug screening and molecular simulations prioritized candidate compounds for further investigation. RESULTS: The support vector machine achieved the best predictive performance for COPD risk (test AUC = 0.821; temporal validation AUC = 0.829). Multi-omics analyses consistently identified IER3 as a central COPD-associated gene within an inflammation-enriched transcriptional network. A six-gene diagnostic signature demonstrated robust external performance (AUC = 0.882 and 0.836), with IER3 and ATF3 emerging as the most reproducible biomarkers across independent cohorts. Single-cell analysis localized IER3 predominantly to airway epithelial cells and macrophages and revealed enhanced epithelial-macrophage communication in COPD. Mendelian randomization supported a causal association between genetically predicted IER3 expression and impaired lung function (IVW beta = -0.042, P < 0.001). Experimental studies further demonstrated that cigarette smoke induced epithelial IER3 expression, whereas IER3 silencing suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production, reduced inflammatory-cell recruitment, alleviated lung injury, and partially restored pulmonary function. Drug-repurposing analysis nominated IMD-0354 as a potential candidate modulator of the IER3-associated inflammatory axis. CONCLUSIONS: We developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for COPD risk prediction and identified IER3 as a candidate mediator of airway epithelial inflammation. Integrated evidence supports its involvement in smoke-induced inflammatory amplification and potential contribution to impaired lung function, highlighting IER3 as a potential therapeutic target warranting further mechanistic and clinical validation.

title: DBP K210 deacetylation suppresses BmNPV proliferation and promotes apoptosis associated with altered BmIAP regulation.
authors: Yang, Siyi; Sun, Yidong; Li, Wenjing; Tariq, Komal; Gao, Jie; Wang, Dajin; Miao, Meng; Yu, Wei
abstract: The DNA-binding protein DBP, encoded by ORF16 of Bombyx mori nucleopolyhedrovirus (BmNPV), is a single-stranded DNA-binding protein expressed early during infection and is essential for efficient viral replication. Although DBP has been proposed to function as a transcriptional regulator, the mechanisms governing its activity remain poorly understood. In our previous study, a quantitative acetylproteomic analysis identified acetylation at lysine 210 (K210) of DBP during BmNPV infection, with its acetylation level increasing approximately 1.7-fold at 36 h post-infection. To investigate the functional significance of this modification, we generated a DBP deficient BmNPV mutant and BmNPV mutants carrying DBP substitutions designed to mimic acetylation or deacetylation at K210. No infectious virus production was detected following loss of DBP, whereas the K210 deacetylation-mimetic mutant showed markedly reduced progeny virus production, accompanied by reduced viral DNA replication and expression of the viral genes examined. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing (ChIP-seq) analysis revealed that the K210 deacetylation-mimetic mutation altered the genomic binding profile of DBP and was associated with changes in host genes involved in apoptosis and cell-cycle regulation. Among them, the binding ability to the apoptosis inhibitor BmIAP decreased after the deacetylation simulation mutation. ChIP-qPCR confirmed DBP enrichment at the IAP promoter, while dual-luciferase assays demonstrated that K210 deacetylation reduced IAP promoter activity. Consistent with these findings, the DBP deacetylation-mimetic mutant increased caspase-3 activity and the expression of the pro-apoptotic genes examined while reducing that of an anti-apoptotic gene. Importantly, overexpression of BmIAP partially attenuated caspase-3 activity and the changes in apoptosis-related transcript levels associated with expression of the DBP deacetylation-mimetic mutant, supporting a contributory role for BmIAP in the observed apoptotic phenotype. Together, these findings support a regulatory role for DBP K210 acetylation in BmNPV replication and suggest that DBP K210 deacetylation is associated with enhanced apoptotic responses, at least partly through modulation of BmIAP expression, providing new insights into the molecular interplay between baculoviruses and their insect hosts.

title: Malva parviflora leaves ameliorated cisplatin nephrotoxicity by targeting PPAR-alpha, HMGB-1/TLR-4, and TNFR-1/RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL axes.
authors: Khalil, Mohammed Nabil Ahmed; Rabie, Mostafa Adel; Mohamed, Ahmed Fathi; Eltanany, Basma Mahmoud; Pont, Laura; Benavente, Fernando; El Motayam, Amira Kamal
journal: The Journal of pharmacy and pharmacology
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the nephroptotective activity of Malva parviflora L. leaves extract (MPLE) against the potent anticancer, cisplatin. METHODS: MPLE was chemically profiled using liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight tandem mass spectrometry and different in vitro analyses. Then, its activity was assessed in vivo model at low and high dose levels (250 and 500 mg/kg). Finally, molecular docking elucidated the key bioactive metabolites in MPLE. KEY FINDINGS: 101 metabolites of diverse chemical classes were identified in MPLE. MPLE had total phenolics and total flavonoids of 10.6 +/- 0.2, 6.5 +/- 0.1 mug gallic acid equivalent/mg extract, mug quercetin equivalent/mg extract, respectively. Moreover, it was effective in different in vitro antioxidant assays. In vivo model, MPLE reduced the elevation in creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, cystatin C and renal content of neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin and kidney injury molecule-1. Mechanistically, MPLE halted oxidative stress, inflammation, and necroptosis by targeting peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-alpha (PPAR-alpha), HMGB-1/TLR-4, and downregulation of TNFR-1/RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL axes, respectively. The ameliorative activity was further supported by the histopathological examination. Molecular docking elucidated that 8-hydroxy flavonoids, e.g. gossypetin and hypolaetin, had a high affinity, to the molecular targets PPAR-alpha, tumor necrosis factor alpha, and tumor necrosis factor receptor 1. CONCLUSIONS: MPLE is a multi-target nephroprotective agent against cisplatin. Further pharmacological and clinical studies are needed before its integration in clinical studies.

title: A Hierarchical KAN-Augmented Graph Convolutional Model for Inferring Cell-Type-Specific Gene Regulations in Single-Cell Omics.
authors: Tang, Binhua; Mao, Mengyao; Wang, Jingyu; Zhou, Fengfeng
abstract: Accurate inference of gene regulatory networks (GRNs) from single-cell RNA-seq data remains challenging due to the complexity of transcription factor (TF)-target interactions and the difficulty in capturing both local and global regulatory dependencies. Here, we present GeneKAN, a novel deep learning framework that integrates multiscale graph convolution with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for robust GRN inference. GeneKAN employs a kernel-based graph convolution module to hierarchically encode gene representations, while KANs model high-order, interpretable TF-target relationships through learnable spline activations. Benchmarking against eleven existing models, and seven scRNA-seq datasets from BEELINE, including diverse cell types, species, and ground-truth networks (ChIP-seq, STRING, LOF/GOF), demonstrates that our proposed GeneKAN achieves state-of-the-art performance in both AUROC and AUPRC. Ablation studies of the proposed model confirm the necessity of each component. Biological validation on human hepatocyte and lung cancer datasets reveals that GeneKAN not only recovers known regulatory interactions with high precision but also identifies functionally relevant hub genes and oncogenic pathways. GeneKAN thus offers a powerful, interpretable, and scalable solution for GRN reconstruction under real-world conditions of data sparsity and noise, with significant potential for advancing systems biology and precision medicine.

title: Neiyi prescription of QIU activates ferroptosis to alleviate endometriosis via tumor protein 53.
authors: Li, Hui; Zhou, Xiaoqing; Mei, Shanshan; Mao, Peiyu; Shi, Xinhe; Yang, Huadi
abstract: Neiyi prescription of QIU (NYPQ) treated endometriosis (Ems). This study aims to explore the molecular mechanism of NYPQ in Ems treatment. Ems model rats were treated with NYPQ (6.3, 12.5 and 25 g/kg), p53 activator (Parthenolide/PTL) and inhibitor (pifithrin-micro/PFTmicro), ferroptosis inhibitor (ferrostatin-1/Fer-1) and inducer (erastin). Hematoxylin-eosin staining, immunohistochemistry, Western blot, and transmission electron microscopes were used for pathology and ferroptosis evaluation. Malondialdehyde (MDA), the System Xc-glutathione, ferrous ion (Fe(2+)) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels were measured using commercial kits. NYPQ activated p53 and ferroptosis signaling pathways in a dose-dependent manner. NYPQ and PTL both decreased lesion volume, glutathione level and expressions of solute carrier family 7 member 11 and glutathione peroxidase 4 while improving tissue pathological damage, activating expressions of p53, prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2, and NADPH oxidase 1, and increasing MDA, Fe(2+) and ROS levels. Additionally, Fer-1 partially reversed the excitatory effects of PTL on ferroptosis. Fer-1 and PFTmicro both exacerbated Ems symptoms meanwhile weakened ferroptosis. Notably, they antagonized improving effect of NYPQ on Ems and activation of ferroptosis. Moreover, the combination of erastin with PFTmicro reversed the inhibition of PFTmicro on NYPQ treating Ems, meanwhile activating ferroptosis. Molecular docking predicted that icariin may interact with p53 and acts as a candidate active component of NYPQ. This study highlights the beneficial effects of p53 signaling pathway activation and NYPQ induced ferroptosis on Ems therapy.

title: Resveratrol Ameliorates Ethanol-Induced Acute Liver Injury in Mice and Primary Hepatocytes by Upregulating the AMPKalpha/Nrf2 Pathway.
authors: Zhang, Cuifeng; Cheng, Min; Lin, Weiqi; Zhang, Xiangyi; Yan, Jingjing; Xie, Xinyi; Xu, Qixiang; Chen, Qun
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is a major global health problem with few effective therapies. Resveratrol (RES) has demonstrated hepatoprotective effects, but its molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that RES protects against ethanol-induced liver injury by activating the AMPKalpha/Nrf2 signaling pathway and upregulating downstream antioxidant enzymes. To test this hypothesis, a comprehensive approach was used, including in vivo and in vitro experiments, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Using C57BL/6 mice and their primary hepatocytes, the therapeutic efficacy of RES in acute alcoholic liver injury. The results showed that RES markedly reduced liver histopathological damage and lessened ethanol-induced hepatocyte injury. These effects may be attributable to its antioxidant activity. RES increased AMPKalpha phosphorylation, as indicated by a higher p-AMPKalpha/AMPKalpha ratio, and promoted Nrf2 nuclear translocation. Concurrently, RES upregulated mRNA and protein levels of heme oxygenase 1 (HO-1) and NADPH quinone oxidoreductase 1 (NQO-1). In primary hepatocytes from Nrf2-/- mice co-cultured with ethanol, HO-1 and NQO-1 levels remained largely unchanged, indicating a critical role for Nrf2 in RES action. Molecular docking studies suggested that RES binds effectively to AMPKalpha and kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1), with docking scores below -5 kcal/mol. Molecular dynamics simulations showed that the RES-Keap1 complex was highly stable, yielding a calculated binding free energy (Deltatotal) of -21.26 +/- 4.41 kcal/mol by MMPBSA analysis. In conclusion, RES improved hepatic function and reduced damage in ALD, potentially by modulating AMPKalpha, Nrf2, HO-1, and NQO1, and thus warrants further investigation for therapeutic application.

title: CKAN-SDBPI: Single-Stranded and Double-Stranded DNA-Binding Protein Identifier Using Convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with Local and Global-Features Fusion.
authors: Arshad, Kamran; Arif, Muhammad; Yu, Dong-Jun
abstract: Single-stranded and double-stranded DNA-binding proteins play essential roles in DNA metabolism, regulation, and genome maintenance; however, accurate computational identification of these proteins remains challenging due to limited feature representation, complex sequence function relationships, and imbalanced classification distributions. Here, we propose CKAN-SDBPI, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates global contextual protein representations with local structural-frequency descriptors for SSB/DSB protein identification. The proposed CKAN-SDBPI employs Ankh protein language model embeddings to capture global sequence information and RECM-DWT descriptors to characterize local structural-frequency patterns. These complementary representations are fused through a Convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (CKAN) to learn nonlinear interactions between heterogeneous feature spaces, while the SMOTETomek strategy is incorporated to improve balanced learning under class imbalance. CKAN-SDBPI was comprehensively evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation, an independent PDB401 test dataset, comparison with existing state-of-the-art predictors, and extensive ablation analyses. CKAN-SDBPI achieved robust predictive performance across validation experiments and demonstrated improved generalization capability on the independent test dataset. The independent evaluation showed that the proposed framework achieved an accuracy of 86.06%, MCC of 0.6238, AUC of 0.8911, and AUPRC of 0.9623. Moreover, ablation studies confirmed the contributions of SMOTETomek-based imbalance handling and CKAN-driven nonlinear feature fusion to the overall performance. Overall, these findings support CKAN-SDBPI as a promising computational method for sequence-based discrimination between SSBs and DSBs.

title: Predicting single-molecule chromatin distribution from DNA sequence.
authors: Wang, Ruoyu; Jin, Junru; Pott, Sebastian; Zhou, Jian
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Genome regulation unfolds through dynamic and stochastic single-molecule events. Deep learning models that read gene regulatory activities from DNA sequences have markedly advanced our ability to predict cell-population-level averages. However, they cannot capture the full spectrum of heterogeneity and dynamics at the single-molecule level, which directly reflect the underlying mechanisms of genome regulation. Here, we introduce a sequence-to-distribution (S2d) framework that directly models the entire probabilistic distribution of single-molecule chromatin states from DNA sequence alone. We used this framework to train Mola, a model of single-molecule chromatin accessibility. We harness Mola to investigate sequence-based regulatory code and mechanisms for multiple aspects of chromatin regulation at the single-molecule level. By quantifying sequence-driven nucleosome regulation, we reveal distinct modes of transcription factor engagement with nucleosomes, including a novel nucleosome-trapping factor, ZNF146. We characterized the sequence determinants governing the +1 nucleosome after transcription start sites and identified YY1 as the strongest +1 nucleosome-positioning factor. Leveraging long-context single-molecule modeling, we further discovered a shared sequence basis for the co-accessibility of regulatory elements and the co-footprinting of transcription factors. Joint prediction of DNA methylation and accessibility reveals a sequence-driven bimodal state mediated by methylation-sensitive transcription factors. Beyond static single-molecule snapshots, the S2d framework can generate pseudo-dynamic trajectories of chromatin states and propose a roadmap toward genome-wide chromatin dynamics. Moreover, we showed that Mola can predict and interpret the effects of genetic variants at the single-molecule level, revealing how sequence changes reshape distal regulatory coordination. Together, this sequence-to-distribution framework lays the foundation for understanding how genomic sequence encodes stochastic and dynamic genome regulation, and how genetic variation changes it, one molecule at a time.

title: Nucleobase-Specific Recognition of DNA by Protamine.
authors: Dhiman, Anshika; Mudiyanselage, Hashini Ekanayake; Zhou, Huan-Xiang
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Protamines-arginine (Arg)-rich, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs)-replace histones to compact DNA in the sperm nucleus. While folded domains can bind DNA site-specifically, whether IDPs exhibit DNA-sequence specificity remains open. Here, we used all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to characterize protamine-DNA binding. Eight copies of salmon protamine (33 residues with 21 Arg) rapidly wrap around a 35-bp DNA molecule. In addition to salt bridges with DNA phosphates, Arg hydrogen-bonds with multiple nucleobases on both strands or the same strand. At the major groove, protamine prefers GC over AT by a 2.6-to-1 ratio, with guanine's O6 and N7 atoms as hydrogen-bond acceptors; the preference is especially strong at G-tracts. This selectivity reverses at the minor groove, where AT overtakes GC by a 2.1-to-1 margin. The net effect is a moderate bias for GC over AT in protamine-base interactions. Additional simulations with 20-bp DNA molecules and free-energy calculations reinforce these observations. For experimental validation, we designed DNA sequences with 0-40% GC content. Protamine-DNA mixtures form aggregates, with an increasing propensity at higher GC content and upon shuffling into G-tracts. This work demonstrates that IDPs can bind DNA in a nucleobase-specific manner, with implications for protamine-mediated transcription silencing and remodeling of paternal chromatin.

title: Machine learning guided design of strong transcriptional activation domains.
authors: Zintel, Marissa A; LeBlanc, Claire J; Kotha, Sanjana R; Soriano, Melvin; Bansal, Rishaan J; Aguilera, Daniel; Majidi, Touss; Ornelas, Izaiah; Kirkpatrick, Liam D; Udupa, Aditya; Hu, Gean; Agarwal, Pooja; Lam, Angelica W Y; Nunez, James K; Shih, Patrick M; Sozzani, Rosangela; Strader, Lucia C; Staller, Max V
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Artificial intelligence has accelerated the design of structured proteins, but it remains difficult to design functional intrinsically disordered proteins because of weak structural constraints and poorly defined sequence-to-function relationships (1) . Activation domains (ADs), transcription factor regions that recruit coactivators, are an excellent test case for the de novo design of intrinsically disordered sequences. ADs are one of the oldest groups of functional intrinsically disordered sequences (2) and designed ADs have applications in synthetic biology, biotechnology, and agriculture. We computationally generated 500,000 candidate sequences that resembled known ADs and predicted AD function with extant machine learning models, including three neural networks. From high-scoring sequences, we selected 18,750 for experimental validation in yeast. Surprisingly, >90% of the 16,770 well-measured sequences function as ADs. Sequences predicted to be active by multiple models were stronger, motivating development of a fast and accurate consensus AD predictor, MADRIGAL. A number of our designed ADs retain functionality across fungi, plants, and human cells. This work illustrates a generalizable paradigm for incorporating sequence-to-function models into the design loop to efficiently generate functional intrinsically disordered sequences.

title: Interplay of diffusive and active motion governs cohesin extrusion and CTCF barrier function.
authors: Tortora, Maxime M C; Fudenberg, Geoffrey
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion constitutes a crucial process for the regulation of chromosome folding and gene expression. A rapidly-growing body of in vitro experiments suggests that cohesin molecular motor activity is finely modulated by both chemical and mechanical cues, whose interplay holds important implications in living cells for development and disease. Yet, biophysical models capable of accurately and efficiently capturing the breadth of reported cohesin behaviors, along with their impacts on DNA spatio-temporal organisation, remain lacking. Here, building on multiple experimental observations of single-cohesin dynamics, we introduce a mesoscale description of cohesin based on the general framework of jump-diffusion processes. We show that the finite stall force of cohesin naturally emerges from the conjunction of active, directional extrusion moves with passive, stochastic drift. The tension-dependent competition between these two orthogonal modes of motion gives rise to highly-heterogeneous cohesin kinetics featuring extrusion, translocation, and loop slipping phases, as observed in vitro . These behaviors are predicted to depend sensitively on both buffer composition and nucleosomal content, reconciling the surprising variability of cohesin kinetics reported across experimental conditions. This jump-diffusion model (JDM) is fully parametrized using available single-molecule measurements and bridges the timescale gap between microscopic stepping events and cohesin regulator association, thus providing mechanistic insights into how CTCF impedes extrusion. Hence, the JDM quantitatively describes force-dependent extrusion in both DNA curtain assays in vitro and in the context of native chromatin for genome folding predictions in nucleo , bridging these previously disparate contexts under a unified numerical and theoretical formalism. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Cohesin folds chromosomes into loops that help regulate gene expression, yet its diverse behaviors and sensitivity to mechanical forces remain largely unexplained. Here, we develop a theory for how competition between active DNA capture and passive sliding governs loop growth, shrinkage, and motion. This framework reconciles seemingly conflicting experimental observations, and predicts how weak forces generated by cohesin on naked DNA in vitro translate into tensions strong enough to drive large-scale genome folding on native chromatin. Jointly considering cohesin mechanics and biochemistry further enables us to explain how the DNA-binding protein CTCF modulates extrusion activity. By connecting single-molecule measurements with chromosome organization mechanisms, we thus provide a quantitative foundation for how physical conditions and regulatory proteins collectively shape genome folding.

title: The SOX9 C-terminus encodes a transferable cBAF-recruitment module for enhancer remodeling and cell-state control.
authors: Raghawan, Akhouri K; Li, Zhixin; Wang, Xiaolu; Huang, Yingbo; Doan, Paul; Gudipudi, Anoushka C; Conway, Caroline; Kositbovornchai, Supakrit; Hsiang, Evan; Lie, Pearl Y P; Cleary, James M; Sethi, Nilay S
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Transcription factors select genomic targets, but how they recruit chromatin remodelers to convert DNA occupancy into cell-state-specific accessibility remains unclear. Here, we identify an intrinsically disordered SOX9 C-terminal module that recruits SMARCB1-containing canonical BAF (cBAF) to stem-like enhancers that open during APC -mutant adenoma formation. Acute, reversible SOX9 degradation displaces cBAF from  approximately 80% of co-bound enhancers, exceeding effects on pBAF and ncBAF, and collapses accessibility and stem-like identity; SOX9 re-expression restores these features. C-terminal truncation preserves DNA binding but disrupts cBAF engagement and chromatin opening. Enforced SMARCB1 docking to truncated SOX9 partially restores cBAF recruitment, accessibility, stem-like transcription, and organoid self-renewal, identifying remodeler recruitment as a limiting effector function. The isolated C-terminus supports higher-order cBAF assembly and, when fused to dCas9 as COMET, redirects endogenous cBAF to targeted loci to open chromatin. Disordered TF regions can therefore encode transferable instructions that deploy specific remodeling complexes to control cell state. HIGHLIGHTS: The SOX9 C-terminal IDR recruits cBAF to adenoma-emergent enhancersSMARCB1 is required for SOX9-dependent enhancer accessibility and stem identity Forced SMARCB1 docking restores stem-like enhancer state and self-renewal to SOX9 (DeltaC) The isolated SOX9 module is sufficient to open chromatin via endogenous cBAF.

title: From network pharmacology to experimental verification: Angelica sinensis and its key constituent beta‑sitosterol exert anti‑liver cancer effects through the p53 signaling pathway.
authors: Du, Ying; Song, Yang; Fan, Yuting; Li, Weitong; Zhang, Yuxin; Shen, Haotian; Tang, Bin; Wang, Jinhui; Deng, Fengmei; Cheng, Li
abstract: Liver cancer remains a major cause of cancer mortality and the limited benefit of existing therapies leaves a clear need for new therapeutic agents. Although Angelica sinensis (AS) shows broad antitumor potential, its mechanistic basis against liver cancer remains unclear. The present study revealed that AS reduced the viability, proliferation and migration of the HepG2 human liver cancer cell line. Network pharmacology pointed to several putative targets including insulin, peroxisome proliferator‑activated receptor gamma, nuclear factor kappaB subunit 1, estrogen receptor 1 and albumin. By combining molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation and Cell Counting Kit‑8 cell viability screening, beta‑sitosterol (BS) was identified from the candidate compounds of AS for further study, based on its stable interactions with central targets and its strong antiproliferative activity against HepG2 cells in vitro. Mechanistic assays of BS revealed that its anti‑liver cancer effect was mediated through the p53 pathway. BS treatment increased the proportion of apoptotic cells, together with increased expression of the tumor suppressor protein p53 and the pro‑apoptotic proteins Bax and Caspase‑3, and reduced expression of the anti‑apoptotic protein Bcl‑2. Co‑treatment with pifithrin‑alpha hydrobromide, a p53 inhibitor, partly reduced the proportion of apoptotic cells and partly reversed these changes in protein expression, confirming a p53‑dependent mechanism. The present study clarified the mechanisms by which AS, and its active component BS, suppress the proliferation and migration of liver cancer cells and trigger apoptosis through the modulation of the p53 pathway. These results support AS and BS as promising leads for development of plant‑derived therapies against liver cancer.

title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal glycolytic remodeling and ENO1-associated metabolic vulnerability in hepatoblastoma.
authors: Wu, Xiongwei; Zhou, Pingping; Wu, Siyan; Zhang, Zhengshou; Jian, Xuemin
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatoblastoma (HB) is the most common malignant liver tumor in children; however, the contribution of glycolytic metabolic reprogramming to HB development and progression remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomic datasets of HB from the GEO database. Glycometabolic pathway activity was quantified using scMetabolism, and pseudotime and transcription factor activity analyses were performed to characterize regulatory programs associated with glycolytic reprogramming. CellChat and spatial transcriptomics were applied to examine predicted tumor-immune communication. hdWGCNA combined with differential expression analysis was used to prioritize glycolysis-associated genes. ENO1 was further evaluated by in silico network perturbation, two independent shRNAs in vitro, and computational compound prioritization followed by molecular docking and a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation. RESULTS: The single-cell atlas resolved 10 major cell types and revealed elevated glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway scores in malignant epithelial cells. Pseudotime analysis showed increasing glycolytic activity along the inferred epithelial trajectory. CellChat predicted enhanced MDK-NCL communication between Glyco_High tumor cells and neutrophils, while spatial analysis showed regional concordance between MDK/NCL co-expression and high-glycolysis areas. hdWGCNA identified three glycolysis-associated candidate genes: ENO1, AKR1A1, and AHCY. In silico ENO1 perturbation was associated with altered inferred regulatory activity of approximately 2.1% of genes. Two independent ENO1-targeting shRNAs produced concordant reductions in proliferation, colony formation, lactate production, and glucose consumption in HepG2 and Huh6 cells. BRD-K14653796 was computationally prioritized, and the modeled ENO1-compound complex remained conformationally stable under the specified simulation conditions. CONCLUSIONS: This study characterizes glycolytic heterogeneity in HB at single-cell and spatial resolution and nominates ENO1 as a candidate metabolic vulnerability in CNV-high putative malignant epithelial cells. It also highlights a computationally predicted MDK-NCL-associated tumor-immune communication pattern and provides testable hypotheses for future preclinical validation.

title: Ellagic acid counteracts ionizing radiation-induced stress resistance decline and lifespan reduction through DAF-16/SKN-1-mediated pathways in C. elegans.
authors: Zhang, Ge; Zhao, Lei; Xuanyuan, Yujie; Han, Zhicheng; Xu, Xiaoying; Mi, Dong; Sun, Yeqing
abstract: Ionizing radiation (IR) exposure in deep space environments has emerged as a serious health concern, as it induces persistent oxidative stress and chronic inflammation, ultimately reducing lifespan. Dietary intervention with natural bioactive compounds presents a promising radioprotective strategy. In this study, we demonstrate that ellagic acid (EA) effectively restores lifespan and enhances stress resistance in Caenorhabditis elegans after extremely high-dose IR exposure. Specifically, EA mitigates reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and reduces oxidative damage levels in C. elegans exposed to high-dose IR, through upregulating antioxidant and innate immune gene expression, and enhancing antioxidant enzyme activity. Molecular docking analyses suggested that EA can probably interact with the transcription factors DAF-16 and SKN-1. Through GFP reporter and loss-of-function experiments, we demonstrated that EA promotes the nuclear accumulation of DAF-16 and SKN-1, thereby triggering downstream antioxidant and immune pathways that collectively enhance stress resistance and mitigate lifespan reduction in C. elegans exposed to high-dose IR. Overall, this work identifies EA as a promising plant-derived natural polyphenolic compound and establish a mechanistic basis for its potential development as a radioprotective intervention.

title: Integration of Network Toxicology and Transcriptomic Data: Exploring Molecular Associations Between Polystyrene Microplastics Exposure and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatohepatitis.
authors: Zhang, Linbing; Wu, Jiarui; Ren, Yuerong; Wang, Xinya; Gao, Qingyao; Sun, Suju
abstract: Polystyrene microplastics (PS-MPs), persistent and bioaccumulative environmental pollutants detected in human tissues, have been increasingly associated with hepatic oxidative stress and inflammatory disturbances; however, their potential molecular relevance in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) remains vague. In this study, we applied a systems-level integrative framework combining transcriptomic analysis, network toxicology, immune profiling, and molecular docking to explore the overlap between genes with curated chemical-gene interactions involving polystyrene in the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) and differentially expressed genes in human MASH liver tissues. By intersecting MASH-associated differentially expressed genes from the Gene Expression Omnibus with polystyrene-related genes curated in the CTD, we identified 80 candidate genes representing an overlap between curated polystyrene-gene interaction records and disease-related transcriptional alterations. Functional enrichment and protein-protein interaction analyses further prioritized eight hub genes (MYC, ATF3, CXCL2, IL18, NOS2, SOD2, FASN, and ARG1) that were consistently associated with inflammatory signaling, oxidative stress regulation, and metabolic dysregulation. Immune infiltration analysis indicated close association of the hub genes expression with characteristic immune remodeling patterns in MASH. Upstream regulatory analysis identified several transcription factors (TFs) potentially involved in coordinating hub gene expression, among which JUN/AP-1 emerged as a central regulatory node linking inflammation, oxidative stress, and metabolism-related programs. Molecular docking analysis provided structural support for the potential physical feasibility of interactions between a polystyrene pentamer and the selected TFs. Collectively, these findings establish a systems-level framework integrating CTD-curated polystyrene-gene interaction information with key transcriptional and immunometabolic features of MASH, generating testable hypotheses about the potential molecular relevance of PS-MPs to MASH for future mechanistic studies and environmental health risk assessment.

title: Time Between Learning Events Shapes Functional Connectivity in Spatial Memory: A Brain-Wide Analysis.
authors: di Sturmeck, Tommaso Gosetti; Bergamo, Sebastiano; Mastrorilli, Valentina; Patrizi, Annarita; Nuzzi, Davide; Pezzulo, Giovanni; Del Ferraro, Gino; Rinaldi, Arianna; Mele, Andrea
abstract: A substantial body of research indicates that spaced training, characterized by longer inter-trial intervals between training epochs, consistently outperforms massed training in promoting durable memory. To investigate the neural mechanisms underlying this difference, we quantified c-Fos expression across 126 brain regions and mapped network activity following both spatial and cue-based learning under massed and spaced training protocols. While both training regimens (spaced and massed) and memory types (spatial and cue-based) produced small-world networks with similar overall topology, they differed in the functional organization of specific circuits. Massed spatial training preferentially activated hippocampal-thalamic and claustrum-basal ganglia-thalamic pathways. In contrast, spaced spatial training promoted stronger cortico-thalamic interactions and enhanced communication between the hippocampus and basal ganglia, indicating a shift toward a more integrated, cortically mediated network. These findings suggest that temporal spacing of training reorganizes memory-related brain networks, enhancing cortical-thalamic dynamics to support more efficient spatial memory. Finally, spaced networks were more sensitive to targeted disruptions of key connector hubs-identified through betweenness centrality analysis-than massed networks, pointing to a potential systems-level trade-off.

title: Solvation-Mediated Effects of Contact Mutations on p53-DNA Binding Dynamics and Energetics.
authors: Gaikwad, Vikram; Venugopal, Pushyaraga P; Chakrabarti, Rajarshi
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
abstract: The tumor suppressor protein p53 is a sequence-specific transcription factor whose DNA-binding domain (DBD) is essential for maintaining genomic stability. Mutations at residues that directly contact DNA frequently impair DNA recognition and are strongly associated with tumorigenesis. In this study, we performed atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate the impact of frequent contact mutations (R248Q, R248W, R273C, and R273H) on the dynamics, energetics, and hydration properties of the p53-DNA complex. Comparative analysis of wild-type (WT) and mutant complexes reveals that these mutations perturb hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interaction networks and alter the solvation environment at the DNA-binding interface, leading to less favorable binding free energies, as quantified by alchemical free energy calculations. Analysis of interfacial water dynamics shows that water molecules in the WT complex are more ordered and long-lived, forming stable water bridges that reinforce protein-DNA contacts. The mutations are accompanied by changes in the interfacial hydration network, including mutation-dependent variations in water-bridge occupancy, water mobility, rotational dynamics, and H-bond relaxation lifetimes. These molecular changes are associated with altered solvation contributions and reduced binding affinity in the mutant systems.

title: Pathomics-based prediction of natural regulatory T cell infiltration in breast cancer.
authors: Xu, Yuanbing; Pan, Yanming; Cui, Manlu; Li, Jingtao; Yang, Qinlian; Huang, Linfei; Pan, Dai; Li, Qiuyun
abstract: BACKGROUND: Natural regulatory T cells (nTregs) are a key immunosuppressive component of the tumor microenvironment (TME), but their assessment typically requires specialized molecular assays. This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning-based pathomics model to predict nTregs infiltration directly from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images (WSI) of breast cancer and evaluate its prognostic significance. METHODS: Data from 1097 breast cancer patients in The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) were analyzed. A cohort of 928 patients with complete RNA-seq data was used to establish the prognostic value of nTregs (estimated by ImmuneCellAI). A subset of 791 patients with matched high-quality H&E-stained WSI was randomly split into training (n = 633) and validation (n = 158) cohorts. A total of 1488 quantitative pathomic features were extracted. After feature selection via minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), a Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) classifier was trained to predict high versus low nTregs status, generating a continuous Pathomics Score (PS). The PS was validated against FOXP3 immunohistochemistry (IHC) and evaluated for its association with overall survival (OS). Multi-omics analyses explored the underlying biology of PS-defined groups. RESULTS: High nTregs infiltration was an independent predictor of poor OS (HR = 1.58, 95% CI 1.10-2.28, p = 0.013). The GBM model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) of 0.81 (95% CI 0.78-0.85) in the training cohort and 0.72 (95% CI 0.63-0.80) in the validation cohort. The PS showed a strong correlation with FOXP3(+) cell density (p < 0.001) and was independently associated with worse OS (HR = 1.68, 95% CI 1.15-2.46, p = 0.008). Patients with high PS exhibited a distinct transcriptomic signature enriched for immune activation pathways (e.g., estrogen responses) and upregulated immune checkpoint genes (e.g., CD276, TNFSF4, TNFSF9), alongside an immunosuppressive microenvironment characterized by increased nTregs and M2-like macrophage estimates. CONCLUSION: We developed and validated a pathomics model that non-invasively predicts nTregs infiltration and patient prognosis from standard H&E images. The PS serves as a novel, accessible digital biomarker that captures the complexity of an inflamed yet immunosuppressive TME and has the potential to augment clinical decision-making, particularly in resource-limited settings.

title: Potential of FGF2 and GIPR as immunological biomarkers and therapeutic targets in recurrent pregnancy loss.
authors: Huang, Liuyi; Wang, Jian; Huang, Hongmei; Huang, Xiaoqin; Huang, Limin; Huang, Huitian; Huang, Fengdie; Wei, Yulan; Dong, Mingyou; Wei, Bixiao
abstract: Recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) is a complex obstetric complication whose immunological mechanisms remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify immune-related biomarkers for RPL by integrating the GSE165004 dataset with immune-related genes from the MSigDB database. A total of 234 immune-related differentially expressed genes (IDEGs) were identified, which were enriched in pathways such as natural killer cell-mediated cytotoxicity, JAK-STAT signaling, and chemokine signaling. Using machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, RF), four hub genes-FGF2, TINAGL1, CKLF, and GIPR-were screened. Among them, FGF2 and GIPR were significantly downregulated in the RPL group (P < 0.05). Diagnostic efficacy was evaluated using ROC curves, and a nomogram was constructed. Immune cell infiltration analysis via CIBERSORT revealed that FGF2 showed a negative correlation with monocyte infiltration, whereas GIPR was positively correlated with resting dendritic cells (P < 0.05), suggesting their involvement in modulating the immune microenvironment. Upstream regulator analysis using NetworkAnalyst predicted that FGF2 may be regulated by miRNAs such as miR-15a-5p, while GIPR was associated with transcription factors SP1/SP3. Validation using single-cell transcriptomics and preliminary clinical samples (RT-qPCR/WB) confirmed the downregulation of FGF2 and GIPR in RPL (P < 0.05). In conclusion, our findings suggest that altered FGF2 and GIPR expression may be associated with immune dysregulation in RPL and warrant further functional investigation. These findings provide preliminary insights for potential immunotherapeutic strategies in RPL, although larger-scale validation and functional studies are needed.

title: MAMTF: a method for predicting transcription factor binding sites combining state-space modeling and adaptive feature fusion.
authors: Zhang, Han; Luo, Junwei; Shen, Xiaohe; Luo, Fen
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) are short sequences on DNA that can be recognized and bound by specific transcription factors (TFs). Accurate identification of TFBSs is crucial for decoding gene regulatory mechanisms and understanding cellular functions. Traditional machine learning-based methods rely on manually designed features, making it difficult to fully uncover the complex patterns within DNA sequences. In recent years, deep learning methods have demonstrated significant advantages in TFBSs prediction. However, existing methods still have shortcomings in terms of local and global feature extraction as well as feature fusion. RESULTS: To address these issues, we propose a deep learning method, MAMTF, designed to integrate local and global DNA features to improve the performance of TFBSs prediction. This method uses a multiscale convolutional neural network to extract local sequence features, employs a bidirectional Mamba architecture to capture long-range dependencies, and designs a cross-gated fusion module to achieve deep interaction between different features. On 165 ChIP-seq datasets encompassing 29 transcription factor (TF) categories, MAMTF achieves a macro-averaged ACC (0.819), ROC-AUC (0.895) and PR-AUC (0.900) over the 29 TF categories, showing promising prediction ability. CONCLUSIONS: Experimental results show that MAMTF outperforms other six methods in predicting TFBSs, exhibiting optimal and stable performance on 29 TF categories, providing a new tool for accurate TFBSs prediction.

title: PIC-NIC reveals that DNA mechanical strain impacts transcription factor recognition.
authors: Yao, Yumi Minyi; O'Hagan, Michael P; Onoon, Karn; Givon, Lihee; Hamer-Rogotner, Shelly; Salinas, Raul; Nithun, Raj V; Kessler, Naama; Jbara, Muhammad; Dym, Orly; Pipatpolkai, Tanadet; Schumacher, Maria A; Afek, Ariel
abstract: DNA is not merely a linear code of bases, but a mechanically constrained polymer whose backbone continuity restricts the conformations accessible during protein recognition. Yet, although base-sequence preferences have been extensively mapped across human transcription factor (TF) families, we lack comparable maps of how TFs read backbone continuity and DNA mechanics, leaving these layers of recognition poorly understood. Here we introduce PIC-NIC, a high-throughput platform that uses site-specific backbone nicks to perturb DNA mechanics while preserving base identity and minimizing accompanying chemical changes. Across 15 TFs spanning eight structural families, PIC-NIC reveals a highly position-dependent response to backbone disruption: most positions are permissive, whereas nicking at mechanically sensitive sites can substantially reshape binding. Mechanistic analyses integrating PIC-NIC maps with freshly determined TF-DNA structures, structural comparisons, binding kinetics and molecular simulations show that sensitive positions often coincide with strain-adapted DNA geometries, including Hoogsteen conformations, whose relaxation can enhance binding or rewire sequence specificity. Genomic single-strand breaks and repair maps further suggest that TF retention at nicked DNA may influence local repair-factor accessibility. Together, these findings systematically map DNA backbone mechanics as a position-resolved layer of TF recognition across diverse protein families, showing how this layer can reshape binding specificity and may influence repair-factor accessibility.

title: Structural basis of TACO1 function in mitochondrial translation elongation.
authors: Singh, Vivek; Gallenstein, Raven; Wanes, George; Shiriaev, Dmitri Igorevich; Shcherbinina, Evgeniia; Gopalakrishna, Shreekara; Amahong, Kuerbannisha; Mohanty, Udayan; Sarshad, Aishe A; Whitford, Paul C; Khawaja, Anas; Rorbach, Joanna
abstract: Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Here, we report the cryo-electron microscopy structure of human TACO1 bound to the mitoribosome, revealing its mechanistic role as a dedicated elongation regulator. Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. It binds near the A site, closely interacting with the Sarcin Ricin loop and the L7/L12 stalk, similar to general translation elongation factors, such as EF-Tumt and mtEF-G1mt, and contacts the A-site tRNA. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

title: Ionization- and iron-tuned recognition of icaritin by albumin and transferrin: from spectrofluorimetry to multiscale modeling.
authors: Milisavljevic, Kristina; Mrkalic, Emina; Kaluderovic, Goran N; Milanovic, Ziko
abstract: Serum transport proteins critically influence the pharmacokinetics and systemic bioavailability of polyphenolic compounds; however, the molecular determinants governing their recognition of ionizable flavonoids remain insufficiently understood. Herein, the interaction of icaritin (ICT), a prenylated flavonoid with promising pharmacological activity, with bovine serum albumin (BSA) and transferrin (Tf) was investigated using an integrated spectrofluorimetric and multiscale computational approach. Fluorescence quenching experiments confirmed stable complex formation with both proteins. ICT exhibited strong affinity toward BSA (Ka = 5.76 x 10(5)-1.12 x 10(7) M(-1)) and Tf (K(a) = 5.07 x 10(7)-2.49 x 10(8) M(-1)), with distinct recognition mechanisms. Site-marker experiments revealed warfarin-dependent changes in the apparent BSA-ICT binding parameters without conclusively identifying a preferred binding site, while Tf binding was strongly influenced by both ligand ionization and iron-loading state. Molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and MM/GBSA-MM/PBSA calculations demonstrated that neutral and monoanionic ICT species predominate under physiological conditions, with the monoanionic form displaying enhanced protein affinity. Additional ONIOM (Our Own N-layered Integrated Molecular Orbital and Molecular Mechanics) QM/MM calculations supported the electronic stabilization of the protein-ligand complexes. The obtained results demonstrate that ICT recognition by BSA and Tf in the investigated model systems depends on ligand ionization, protein architecture and the iron-loading state of transferrin, providing a molecular basis for understanding ICT-protein interactions and their potential relevance to serum protein binding.

title: Exploring the role of HNF1B in the pathogenesis of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD): an integrative bioinformatics study.
authors: Cao, Wenlong; Yao, Ye; Chen, Yiwen; Wang, Yuqin; Xiong, Jing
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hepatocyte nuclear factor 1 beta (HNF1beta) is crucial for renal tubule development, and its mutation causes renal cysts. However, its role in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) remains unclear. This study explored the mechanism of hepatocyte nuclear factor 1-beta gene (HNF1B) in ADPKD using integrative bioinformatics analysis. METHODS: HNF1B expression was evaluated in ADPKD transcriptome datasets and validated via immunofluorescence in a 3D Madin-Darby canine kidney cell cyst model cultured over a 12-day timeframe (analyzed on days 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12). Based on HNF1B median expression, ADPKD tissues were divided into high- and low-expression groups for differential and enrichment analyses. Upstream transcription factors and binding sites were predicted using UCSC and JASPAR databases. Finally, cMAP and L1000FWD were used to screen therapeutic small molecules targeting HNF1beta, followed by molecular docking. RESULTS: HNF1B was significantly downregulated in ADPKD tissues (p = 0.017) and correlated with cyst progression (p < 0.001), which was consistent with the 3D model findings (p < 0.001). Low HNF1B expression was associated with transcriptomic signatures reflecting activation of the wingless-related integration site (Wnt) and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-beta) pathways and inhibition of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) pathway. POU3F3, HNF4A, and TFAP2B were identified as potential upstream transcription factors. Mocetinostat (binding energy = -8.2 kcal/mol) and wortmannin (binding energy = -7.7 kcal/mol) showed stable binding to HNF1beta. CONCLUSION: HNF1B expression is significantly negatively correlated with cyst progression, suggesting a potential protective role in ADPKD, and its downregulation associates with pathways driving cyst progression.

title: [Mechanisms of Shenghui Decoction in activating PPARalpha to promote microglial phagocytosis and degradation of Abeta].
authors: Wang, Yu-Min; Wang, Min; Huang, Yan-Li; Xu, Dai-Yu; Gao, Gai; Zhang, Xiao-Wei; Zhang, Zhen-Qiang; Xie, Zhi-Shen
journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
abstract: This study aimed to elucidate the potential mechanisms by which Shenghui Decoction(SHD) promotes microglial cells to phagocytose and degrade surrounding deposited beta-amyloid protein(Abeta) through the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha(PPARalpha)/transcription factor EB(TFEB) signaling pathway. Multiple approaches, including Western blot, real-time quantitative PCR(RT-qPCR), molecular docking, reporter gene assays, and immunofluorescence, were employed for verification. Mouse microglial cells(BV2 cells) were divided into the control group, model group, positive control(WY14643) group, and SHD low-, medium-, and high-dose groups(50, 100, and 200 mug.mL~(-1)), respectively. An Abeta-induced BV2 cell injury model was established, and different reagents were added according to group assignment. BV2 cell viability was assessed using the MTT assay. Fluorescently labeled Abeta_(1-42)(FAM-Abeta_(1-42))was used to evaluate Abeta phagocytosis and degradation in each group. Reporter gene assays were performed to determine the transcriptional activities of PPARalpha and TFEB. RT-qPCR was conducted to detect the expression of low-density lipoprotein receptor(LDLR), autophagy-related genes 5 and 7(Atg5 and Atg7), and lysosome-associated membrane protein 2(LAMP2). Western blot was used to determine the expression levels of PPARalpha, LDLR, TFEB nuclear translocation, microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 Ⅰ and Ⅱ(LC3Ⅰ and LC3Ⅱ), P62, and LAMP2 proteins. Immunofluorescence was employed to further validate TFEB nuclear translocation. Molecular docking analysis was conducted to evaluate the binding between SHD active constituents and the ligand-binding domain of PPARalpha. The results showed that SHD had no significant effect on BV2 cell viability at concentrations of 50-300 mug.mL~(-1). SHD enhanced Abeta phagocytosis and degradation, upregulated LDLR expression, significantly increased the nuclear translocation and expression levels of PPARalpha and nuclear TFEB proteins, and enhanced the transcriptional activities of PPARalpha and TFEB. SHD significantly upregulated the expression of the autophagy-related genes Atg5 and Atg7 and the lysosome-related gene LAMP2, increased the protein expression levels of LC3Ⅱ/LC3Ⅰ and LAMP2, and significantly decreased P62 protein expression. Molecular docking results indicated that 50 active constituents in SHD could bind to the ligand-binding domain of PPARalpha and form stable hydrogen bonds, with binding energies <-5 kcal.mol~(-1). In summary, SHD improves the autophagic-lysosomal function in BV2 cells, thereby facilitating the phagocytosis and degradation of Abeta. This underlying mechanism is likely associated with the activation of the PPARalpha/TFEB signaling pathway.The findings of this study help elucidate the modern scientific connotation of SHD and may provide a rational therapeutic strategy for the clinical prevention and treatment of Alzheimer's disease.

title: [Mechanism of Jiangxinwei Compound improving chronic obstructive pulmonary disease by regulating ferroptosis based on network pharmacology and experimental validation].
authors: Chen, Cheng-Ye; Yu, Li-Qiu; Sun, Xin; Wei, Jian-Lin; Li, Meng-Fan; Cui, Wen-Jie; An, Xue-Jing; Zhang, Jia-Yu; Wang, Zhui-En; Yang, Yi
journal: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
abstract: Based on network pharmacology and molecular docking, this study investigated the mechanism of action of Jiangxinwei Compound, which was composed of Zingiberis Rhizoma, Asari Radix et Rhizoma, and Schisandrae Chinensis Fructus. Through dually targeting the glycogen synthase kinase-3beta(GSK-3beta)/nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2(NRF2)/glutathione peroxidase 4(GPX4) axis, and prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2(PTGS2), the compound inhibited ferroptosis, enhanced antioxidant capacity, and alleviated chronic obstructive pulmonary disease(COPD). In this study, a COPD rat model was established by combining lipopolysaccharide(LPS) and cigarette smoke(CS). Forty-eight rats were randomly divided into a blank group, a model group, a dexamethasone group, and Jiangxinwei Compound groups with low, medium, and high doses, with eight rats per group. After intervention, body weights, lung function, histopathology, inflammatory markers, and ferroptosis markers were assessed. Western blot and immunofluorescence were used to detect the protein expressions of PTGS2, phosphorylated-GSK-3beta(p-GSK-3beta), NRF2, and GPX4 in lung tissue, while real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction(RT-qPCR) was used to measure the corresponding mRNA levels. The results show that, compared with the model group, the Jiangxinwei Compound groups exhibit significantly improved lung function, alleviated pathological injury of lung tissue, reduced levels of the inflammatory cytokines, such as interleukin-6(IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-alpha(TNF-alpha) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF), decreased levels of ferroptosis markers including reactive oxygen species(ROS), malondialdehyde(MDA), and ferrous ion(Fe~(2+)) in lung tissue, and increased level of the antioxidant indicator reduced glutathione(GSH). Western blot and qPCR also reveal that the Jiangxinwei Compound downregulates PTGS2 expression and upregulates p-GSK-3beta, NRF2, and GPX4 expression. The RT-qPCR results show that Jiangxinwei Compound downregulates the mRNA expression of PTGS2 and upregulates those of NRF2 and GPX4. In summary, the Jiangxinwei Compound effectively ameliorates lung dysfunction and inflammation in COPD rats, and its mechanism of action may involve dual targeting of the GSK-3beta/NRF2/GPX4 axis and PTGS2, thereby inhibiting ferroptosis and enhancing antioxidant capacity in lung tissue.

title: Exploring the mechanism of oxfendazole in inhibiting osteosarcoma-induced osteolysis based on single-cell RNA seqsuencing.
authors: Miao, Jifeng; Wang, Pintian; Feng, Wenyu; Quan, Haiyi; Lin, Yunhua; Wei, Gejin; Meng, Fake; Li, Shanhang; Yang, Mingxiu; Ning, Binyuan; Deng, Jingxin; Xiong, Liang; Hu, Jianming; Liu, Yun; Wei, Qingjun
abstract: Osteosarcoma-associated osteolysis represents a major obstacle in the management of osteosarcoma. Within the osteolytic microenvironment, interactions between osteoclasts and tumor cells facilitate tumor proliferation and metastatic dissemination, and contribute to the development of pathological fractures. However, conventional osteoclast-targeting agents are insufficient to effectively suppress osteosarcoma-driven bone resorption. In this study, single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify critical regulators involved in osteoclast differentiation in the context of osteosarcoma. Using the Beyondcell platform, drugs targeting osteoclast-related signaling pathways were screened, and oxfendazole (OFN) was identified as a potential therapeutic candidate, with ANXA2 recognized as a key associated target. In vitro osteoclastogenesis assays and an in vivo tibial orthotopic osteosarcoma model demonstrated that oral administration of OFN via gavage effectively suppressed osteoclast formation and osteolytic activity, as confirmed by micro-CT and histopathological analyses. But OFN alone did not significantly inhibit osteosarcoma growth but effectively reduced osteoclast-mediated osteolysis. In addition, qRT-PCR and immunohistochemistry confirmed that OFN downregulates ANXA2 expression in vitro and in vivo, thereby impairing osteoclast differentiation. Molecular dynamics simulations combined with in-vitro validation further suggested that OFN may interact with the transcription factor ZNF530, leading to reduced ANXA2 transcription. In conclusion, the integration of single-cell RNA sequencing with the Beyondcell algorithm enabled the identification of OFN as a potent candidate agent for osteosarcoma-induced osteolysis. OFN attenuates osteoclastogenesis and bone resorption by suppressing ANXA2 expression. These findings provide preclinical evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of OFN in the treatment of osteosarcoma-associated osteolysis.

title: Evolution, information content, and optimality of gene regulatory architectures.
authors: Barton, Nicholas H; Tkacik, Gasper
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Evolution of genetic regulatory sequences is shaped by their genotype-phenotype map, but this map itself can evolve via changes in the molecular machinery that reads out the regulatory sequences. Using population genetics theory, we derive a maximization principle, which implies that genotype-phenotype maps will evolve to associate fit phenotypes with larger numbers of possible genotypes. Mathematically, this builds on analogies between population genetics and statistical physics, as well as optimal coding in information theory. The results are particularly interesting in the context of transcriptional regulation, where optimal values of certain parameters that determine the gene regulatory architecture can be derived even without a complete knowledge of the molecular mechanisms involved. We illustrate the theory using a simplified model of transcription factor (TF) binding to cis-regulatory elements (CREs): the fraction of possible CREs across the entire genotype space that bind a given TF evolves to match the fraction of CREs under selection to bind that TF. Similar "frequency matching" results are expected to emerge generically, because selection implicitly moves the entire regulatory architecture toward a fitness maximum, determining the "replicated genotype-phenotype map" for all CREs, while it simultaneously adapts toward individually fit CREs on that map. We discuss the subtleties and limitations of the theory related to biophysical constraints and the need for mutational robustness. Last, our theory suggests a possible mathematical definition for evolvability with predictive power that can be tested in evolutionary simulations and, ultimately, in comparative genetics studies.

title: Molecular interactions underlying selective partitioning of clients into MED1 and FUS condensates.
authors: Yasuda, Ikki; Yamamoto, Eiji; Yasuoka, Kenji; Lindorff-Larsen, Kresten
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
abstract: Biomolecular condensates selectively recruit and exclude proteins, and this partitioning is sometimes dictated by their intrinsically disordered regions. Factors that determine partitioning include client-scaffold interactions and stabilization of the scaffold network within the condensate, yet a molecular and predictive understanding has not been fully achieved. Here, we used coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations to elucidate molecular interactions between two types of nuclear proteins as scaffolds: the charge-rich disordered region of Mediator 1 (MED1) and the aromatic-rich disordered region of Fused in Sarcoma (FUS), in mixtures with client intrinsically disordered regions from six different proteins. We show distinct partitioning into the MED1 and FUS condensates, while the presence of RNA in both dilute and dense phases modulated client partitioning. Favorable client-scaffold interaction energies within condensates were associated with client partitioning, while client-scaffold interactions competed with scaffold self-interactions. Analysis of interaction energies of individual residues revealed that the interactions were localized to specific sequence regions: charged blocks for interactions with MED1, and dispersed aromatic residues for interactions with FUS. Using residue-resolved interaction energies from our molecular dynamics simulations, we developed sequence-based predictors of client partitioning into MED1 and FUS condensates. Our prediction approach for partitioning can be extended to other biomolecules, offering a framework to analyze their partitioning in cellular environments.

title: Live-cell imaging reveals two modes of TERRA association with telomeres and the dynamics of TERRA R-loops.
authors: Kyriacou, Eftychia; Voigt, Franka; Lunardi, Thomas; Dominguez Mantes, Albert; Weigert, Martin; Chao, Jeffrey A; Lingner, Joachim
abstract: Telomeres are transcribed into TERRA long non-coding RNAs. When associating with telomeres, TERRA can regulate telomere maintenance by semiconservative DNA replication, telomerase and homology-directed repair (HDR). In addition, TERRA alters telomeric structure and protein composition. Yet, the molecular mechanisms and dynamics by which TERRA associates with telomeres remain elusive. To investigate TERRA-telomere interactions, we combine PP7 stem-loop TERRA tagging, genome editing and live-cell imaging. Using a deep-learning method for spot detection and single-particle tracking analysis, we demonstrate that TERRA associates with telomeres through two distinct modes. On one hand, TERRA interacts frequently and transiently with the telomeric shelterin protein TRF2. On the other hand, TERRA engages in long-lasting interactions which persist from seconds to several minutes forming R-loops with telomeric DNA. TERRA R-loops preferentially occur at short telomeres, and their formation requires factors involved in HDR, but not TRF2. Altogether, we reveal two parallel mechanisms of TERRA recruitment to telomeres, which differ substantially in their dynamics and structure, and we elucidate the dynamics of telomeric R-loops. Our findings provide a framework for understanding TERRA-triggered telomere functions during aging and carcinogenesis.

title: Predictive modeling of single-cell transcriptomic dynamics with Dynamo.
authors: Zeng, Zehua; Yu, Sichao; Ni, Ke; Zhang, Yan; Shin, Ukyeon; Huang, Cinlong; Cao, Natalie; Weissman, Jonathan; Ellison, David; Xing, Jianhua; Qiu, Xiaojie
abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) provides a powerful means to investigate cell fate dynamics during development and disease. However, existing computational approaches-such as RNA velocity-are often limited to qualitative and descriptive insights. We previously presented Dynamo, a machine learning framework that leverages noisy RNA velocity estimates to learn analytical and predictive vector fields of gene expression dynamics. These learned vector fields enable a suite of novel, quantitative analyses, including mapping the geometry of cell state transitions, identifying dynamic features of differentiation trajectories, inferring gene regulatory networks, predicting optimal paths and transcription factor cocktails for cellular reprogramming, and simulating in silico genetic perturbations. Here we provide a comprehensive protocol for applying Dynamo across four distinct data types and five downstream analyses, demonstrating its versatility in handling conventional and metabolic-labeling-enabled scRNA-seq, multiomic datasets and even datasets without velocity information. We also show that Dynamo can predict cell fate diversions following genetic perturbations and accurately identify key transcription factors that enable lineage transitions in the hematopoietic system. By enabling predictive modeling from single-cell data, our protocol aims to empower the development of generative and predictive models of single-cell genomics. While typical RNA velocity vector field analyses can be completed in less than an hour, the nine case studies in the Protocol can be completed in ~7 h and 35 min. The Protocol is designed for researchers with basic familiarity in scRNA-seq analysis and Python programming, although no advanced coding expertise is required.

title: Hepatoprotective effects of neohesperidin against acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury through modulation of EGFR signaling.
authors: Lai, Shanglei; Fu, Ai; Dong, Fan; Yu, Jundi; Wang, Keyi; Zeng, Yibo; Ding, Bin; Yu, Wangqin; Ding, Qinchao
abstract: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a major cause of acute liver injury (ALI), yet effective therapies remain limited. Neohesperidin (Neo), a citrus-derived flavonoid glycoside, has recognized antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, but its role in APAP-induced hepatotoxicity is unclear. Here, APAP-induced ALI mice and APAP-treated AML12 hepatocytes were used to evaluate the hepatoprotective effects of Neo. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were performed to explore potential targets, and epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) signaling was further examined using pharmacological activation and gene silencing. Neo markedly alleviated APAP-induced liver injury, as shown by reduced alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels, improved histopathology, and enhanced hepatocyte viability. Neo also restored redox homeostasis, increased antioxidant enzyme activities, reduced reactive oxygen species accumulation, attenuated inflammatory responses, and suppressed endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress via the protein kinase R-like ER kinase (PERK)- activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4) pathway. Mechanistically, EGFR was identified as a potential target associated with Neo-mediated protection. Neo reduced APAP-induced EGFR phosphorylation in vivo and in vitro, whereas EGFR activation largely abolished its protective effects. EGFR silencing also alleviated APAP-induced hepatocyte injury. Overall, Neo protects against APAP-induced ALI, at least partly through modulation of EGFR signaling, accompanied by attenuation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and ER stress.

title: Toddalolactone inhibits the activation of fibroblasts in skin fibrosis by regulating MAOA.
authors: Wang, Yongping; Li, Shimeng; Song, Hao; Yang, Cheng
abstract: Skin fibrosis is characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix driven by activated fibroblasts, leading to varying degrees of patient discomfort, deformity, disability, and even death. In vitro studies using mouse primary skin fibroblasts (PSFs) and patient-derived primary keloid fibroblasts (KFs) demonstrated that toddalolactone (Tod) significantly inhibited fibroblast proliferation, migration, and activation and suppressed the TGF-beta1/Smad and TGF-beta1/non-Smad pathways in these cells. In a bleomycin (BLM)-induced mouse model of skin fibrosis, Tod treatment significantly reduced dermal thickness and collagen deposition in mouse skin, decreased skin hydroxyproline content, and inhibited fibroblast activation as well as the TGF-beta1/Smad and TGF-beta1/non-Smad pathways in vivo. In a keloid xenograft mouse model, Tod treatment significantly reduced the relative weight of keloids in mice. Histopathological analysis revealed that Tod alleviated the degree of keloid fibrosis and collagen aggregation while inhibiting fibroblast activation in keloid tissue. Furthermore, molecular docking identified monoamine oxidase A (MAOA) as a potential target of Tod. Cellular thermal shift assays and MAOA knockdown using siRNA in PSFs and KFs demonstrated that Tod inhibits the TGF-beta1 pathway and suppresses fibroblast activation by inhibiting MAOA. Collectively, the findings reveal that Tod regulates the TGF-beta1/Smad and TGF-beta1/non-Smad pathways through inhibiting MAOA, thereby affecting skin fibroblast activation and alleviating skin fibrosis.

title: GPCR-Mediated Regulation of Cytochrome P450 Drives Sulfoxaflor Resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover.
authors: Lv, Haixiang; Li, Xuchao; Yang, Chengzhi; Guo, Zhimin; Huang, Yang; He, Shun; Wan, Hu; Li, Jianhong; Bass, Chris; Ma, Kangsheng
abstract: Rapid evolution of insecticide resistance threatens agricultural productivity. While the fundamental molecular and biochemical mechanisms underlying resistance are well documented, the regulatory processes governing resistance-associated genes, particularly those involving signal-regulated transcription factors, remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated trans-regulation of cytochrome P450 genes associated with sulfoxaflor resistance in Aphis gossypii Glover. Our findings suggest that G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR)-associated signaling and cAMP response element binding protein contribute to resistance-associated P450 gene regulation. FISH and RT-qPCR demonstrate that DopR1 transcripts are enriched in the epidermis, and beta-1A transcripts are enriched in the head. Molecular docking, heterologous expression, and biolayer interferometry assays demonstrate that DopR1 and beta-1A participate in cellular recognition or response to sulfoxaflor and activate downstream cAMP signaling. Silencing DopR1 and beta-1A reduced cAMP content, PKA activity, P450 enzyme activity, and resistance-related P450 expression, thereby enhancing aphid sensitivity to sulfoxaflor. Inhibitor-based suppression, pathway gene silencing, and dual-luciferase reporter assays implicated AC-2, AC-5, PKA-4, PKA-7, CRTC, and CREB in regulating critical resistance-related genes, especially CYP6CY19. Furthermore, functional validation using transgenic Drosophila melanogaster expressing CYP6CY13 and CYP6CY19 demonstrated increased sulfoxaflor tolerance. Collectively, these findings support a working model linking GPCR-associated signaling to the regulation of selected resistance-associated P450 genes in A. gossypii.

title: Integrative computational evaluation of tazemetostat for ARID1A-deficient anaplastic thyroid cancer via predicted polypharmacology and epigenetic target engagement.
authors: Haoyong, Zhang; Cheng, Qian
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) is a rare, highly aggressive malignancy with limited therapeutic options, due largely to rapid metastasis and treatment resistance. A potential vulnerability in a subset of ATC cases is the loss of ARID1A, a core subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex, which induces a synthetic lethal dependency on EZH2, the catalytic subunit of the opposing PRC2 complex. Although tazemetostat was previously approved for selected cancers, recent safety concerns and market withdrawal have limited its direct clinical applicability; nevertheless, it remains a clinically characterized EZH2 inhibitor useful for mechanistic interrogation of ARID1A-EZH2 dependency. This study used tazemetostat as a mechanistic computational probe to evaluate EZH2-centered vulnerability and predicted protein interactions in ARID1A-deficient thyroid cancer. RESULTS: Through network pharmacology, we identified five hub targets central to ARID1A-deficient thyroid cancer progression: EZH2, EGFR, MAPK1, GSK3B, and CYP3A4. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding of tazemetostat to all targets, with docking scores ranging from DeltaG =  - 9.04 kcal/mol (EZH2) to - 13.27 kcal/mol (EGFR). Triplicate molecular dynamics simulations supported overall pose stability across the five complexes, with target-dependent inter-replica variability. Statistical analysis indicated the strongest inter-replica consistency for EZH2 and MAPK1, whereas CYP3A4, EGFR, and GSK3B showed significant replica-level differences despite maintaining stable overall trajectory behavior. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings support tazemetostat as a mechanistic computational probe for investigating EZH2-centered vulnerability in ARID1A-deficient anaplastic thyroid cancer, with predicted binding to EZH2 and additional cancer-relevant proteins. These results suggest potential polypharmacology; however, docking and MD simulations demonstrate binding stability rather than confirmed functional inhibition or pathway modulation. Experimental validation will be required to establish the biological significance of these predicted interactions.

title: Decomposing multi-scale dynamic regulation from single-cell multiomics with scMagnify.
authors: Chen, Xufeng; Yan, Xi; Shen, Bihan; Wang, Heqi; Tang, Zhixuan; Zang, Yan; Lin, Ping; Zhang, Haibing; Li, Yu; Li, Hong
abstract: Deciphering the highly coupled regulatory circuits that drive cellular dynamics remains a fundamental goal in biology. However, capturing the multi-scale time-lagged dynamics and combinatorial regulatory logic of gene regulation remains challenging. Here we present scMagnify, a deep-learning-based framework that leverages chromatin accessibility and gene expression via Granger causality to reconstruct and decompose multi-scale gene regulatory networks (GRNs). Diverse benchmarks demonstrate scMagnify's favorable performance. scMagnify employs tensor decomposition to identify combinatorial TF modules and their activation profiles across multiple time-lags. We applied scMagnify to human hematopoiesis and mouse pancreas development, where it recovered known lineage-driving regulators and provided further insights into the combinatorial logic underlying cell fate decisions. Furthermore, in the context of kidney injury, scMagnify's intercellular communication module mapped key signaling-to-transcription cascades linking microenvironment cues to pathological epithelial cell changes. In summary, scMagnify provides a robust computational framework for dissecting the multi-scale regulatory logic that governs complex biological processes in development and disease.

title: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor cytoplasmic retention by p27;Kip1 in senescent astrocytes.
